steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, exactly 5 years after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand. It was primarily negotiated by three leaders: Wilson (USA), Clemenceau (France), and Lloyd George (Britain). Their conflicting aims made a balanced settlement almost impossible.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Treaty of Versailles had five main categories: War Guilt, Reparations, Military restrictions, Territorial losses, and the League of Nations. Germans called it the "Diktat" (dictated peace) because they were not allowed to negotiate the terms.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Germany lost 13% of its European territory, 10% of its population, and all of its overseas empire. The "Polish Corridor" was particularly resented because it separated East Prussia from the rest of Germany and placed millions of ethnic Germans under Polish rule.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Germans called the Treaty a "Diktat" (dictated peace) because they were given no opportunity to negotiate. The German delegation was shown the terms on 7 May 1919 and told to sign within 15 days. When they proposed modifications, the Allies rejected all significant changes. The German government initially refused to sign, but agreed after the Allies threatened to invade.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two reasons why Clemenceau wanted a harsh treaty. (4 marks) | How far were the Big Three satisfied with the Treaty of Versailles? (8 marks) | "The Treaty of Versailles was completely unfair to Germany." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the exact date: Treaty signed 28 June 1919 - 5 years after Franz Ferdinand's assassination Always use the five categories: War Guilt, Reparations, Military, Territory, League of Nations Reparations were £6.6 billion (132 billion gold marks) - set in 1921, not 1919 For "fair/unfair" questions, always give BOTH sides before making a judgement The Brest-Litovsk comparison is powerful: Germany imposed harsher terms on Russia in March 1918 Article 231 is NOT the same as reparations - it's the WAR GUILT clause that PROVIDED the basis for reparations The USA never joined the League - this is crucial for explaining the League's later failures
